3.text: giving festivals. The essential features are as follows.

4.text: The boats that took part in the hunt pass around the carcass while it

5.text: is still in the water, following the direction of the sun’s course. The owners

6.text: of the boats exclaim, “Yoho, yoho!” the usual cry at the Chukchee ceremo-

7.text: nials. When the carcass is landed on the shore, another procession is formed,

8.text: which likewise passes around the animal. The owner of the boat from which

9.text: the whale received the fatal stroke heads this procession, and after him comes

10.text: the man who gave the death-blow to the whale. All the men who chance

11.text: to be on shore during the landing take part in the parade, and each one

12.text: exclaims, “Yoho, yoho!” Then the women appear and join in the procession,

13.text: which passes again around the carcass. The women repeat incantations

14.text: having for their aim the conciliation of the whale and the acquisition of his

15.text: influence in inciting his mates to come to the shore in future.

16.text: After that the general carving of the meat follows, in which the inhabi-

17.text: tants of all neighboring villages and camps may take part, if they arrive in

18.text: season to do so. Meanwhile, however, the women comprising the household

19.text: of the owner of the boat from which the whale was killed cut bits from the

20.text: ends of his flippers, his nose, and both lips. They take also his eyes and

21.text: some of the shortest whalebone, not good for sale, and they chop besides a

22.text: few pieces from the longer bone. All these are placed on a skin, and are

23.text: supposed to represent the whole of the whale.

24.text: The skin with the scraps on it is brought up to the house, where “the

25.text: whale” is “given a drink” before the entrance; that is, it receives a libation

26.text: of warm water, as is usual with larger game. Sacrifice is also offered to it

27.text: with sausage and reindeer-meat. Then the skin and the particles are carried

28.text: inside the house and put on the roof of the sleeping-room, near its front.

29.text: In the case of a bear the carcass is skinned; but the head, the neck,

30.text: and the shoulders are left with the skin. This receives a “drink” before the

31.text: entrance, and a sacrifice of sausage, and then is brought into the house and

32.text: into the sleeping-room, where it is put on the master’s side and in the place

34.text: A big lamp burns all the time near the symbolized game; also a piˊntᴇ

35.text: fire, which figures in all the ceremonials of the Chukchee. The “whale” and

36.text: the “bear” remain in their respective places five days and nights, and all

37.text: this time the most careful attention is lavished on them. Men and women

38.text: make them presents of their bead necklaces, which are hung over the “bear’s”

39.text: neck, or laid at the side of the “whale.” They receive frequent libations of

40.text: water, and sacrifices of various meats; and neither of them is left alone for

41.text: a moment in the house. The natives say, “The guest will feel lonely.”

42.text: Every kind of loud noise is forbidden, lest “the guest should be awakened
